name: GTE-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct
attention_variant: causal decoder (Qwen2) used as a bi-encoder via last-token pooling
notes: THE EXCEPTION in the embedding slice: this embedder is a CAUSAL DECODER, so unlike every other record here it DOES have a KV cache by construction, and the formula applies. head_dim derived = 1536 / 12 = 128. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 28 * 2 * 128 * 2 * 2 = 14336 bytes/token at bf16 — small, because Qwen2 GQA here is 12 query / 2 KV heads. But for embedding use it is IRRELEVANT: embedding is a single forward pass with last-token pooling, the cache is never grown, so resident memory is dominated by the 1.78B weights, not by KV. Recording the number anyway because the architecture is a decoder and a serving stack that sizes memory by the KV formula will get a wrong answer for this model. Serving profile: 32x the compute of a BERT-base embedder (3.55e9 vs 2.19e8 flops/token) and 5x the parameters of bge-large. It exists because it scores materially better on retrieval benchmarks and handles 131072 max_position_embeddings natively (sliding_window 131072, effectively disabled, rope_theta 1e6). The cost is that it is GPU-class work — unlike bge-small, this one is not faster on CPU. Vocab 151646 dominates the parameter count: 151646 * 1536 = 233M of the 1.776B is the embedding table. Apache-2.0. GGUF ports exist (second-state, gaianet) and ONNX (AnotherWallace/keisuke-miyako int8, twright8 fp16) — the int8 GGUF and ONNX builds are the practical CPU story for this class.
